beats.text: Five opening lines that hook you from the very first breath.
One. "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times." — A Tale of Two Cities, Dickens.
Two. "Call me Ishmael." Three words, and Melville's Moby-Dick has you.
Three. "It is a truth universally acknowledged..." — Austen opens Pride and Prejudice with a smirk.
Four. "Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way." — Tolstoy.
Five. "I am a sick man. I am a spiteful man." — Dostoevsky's Notes from Underground.
A great first line is a promise. These five keep it. Which hooked you hardest?
